retrieved_from: Ported byte-for-byte from Chemclaw3's `src/chemclaw/science/safety/ich_q3d.yaml`, transcribed there by hand from ICH Q3D(R2), 'Guideline for Elemental Impurities', ICH Step 4, 2022 — Appendix 2, Table A.2.1 (Permitted Daily Exposures for Elemental Impurities). Nothing is fetched at runtime and no address here is read by any code.
description: 21 elements with their Q3D class and their oral, parenteral and inhalation PDEs in micrograms per day, plus what each class means. THREE DELIBERATE OMISSIONS TRAVEL WITH THIS FILE AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED. (1) Ag, Au and Ni are ABSENT: Q3D(R2) revised those three entries and the transcriber could not verify the revised numbers against the source, so each returns a miss saying 'read the guideline' rather than a guessed PDE — nickel in particular is a real element with a real limit that this table does not carry, which is exactly what the miss verdict has to say. (2) The cutaneous and transcutaneous routes introduced by Q3D(R2) are absent; only Table A.2.1's three routes are here. (3) The 'other elements' of Q3D section 4 (Al, B, Ca, Fe, K, Mg, Mn, Na, W, Zn) are absent because the guideline establishes no PDE for them — inventing a row saying 'no limit' would read as a clearance. A PDE is an exposure limit for the drug product, not a specification for an intermediate and not a control strategy.
